# PR Review Sweep -- reference detail

Companion to `SKILL.md`. Read the section a step points to; every normative rule stays in `SKILL.md`.

## Inputs (full)

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SCOPE` | string[] | Repository-relative paths, directories or globs. `['.']` sweeps the whole repository. An empty or unreadable scope is an error, never "everything by default". |
| `SWEEP_SHA` | string | The commit being swept -- a full 40- or 64-hex object id (the HEAD commit id of the branch under review), never a bare ref. Guidance is read from THIS commit: a sweep reviews merged code, so the merged tree is also the guidance in force (REQ-024). |
| `REQUESTED_BY` | string | A maintainer's login, or the host automation's identity (for example `github-actions[bot]`). Recorded in the report; it never changes what is reviewed. |
| `TIER` | `'low'` \| `'medium'` \| `'high'` (optional) | Absent means `high` -- a sweep nobody bounded gets the deepest review, never the cheapest. |
| `MAX_PATHS` | number (optional) | Ceiling on paths examined, so a large repository can be swept in parts. The report names what was left; a truncated sweep is never reported as complete. |
| `TEST_COMMAND` | string (optional) | Recorded for reproduction instructions only. A sweep runs no tests and changes nothing. |

## Step 1 -- the sweep set

List files under `SCOPE` at `SWEEP_SHA` from that commit's tree listing (paths, and sizes from the long form of the same listing). A path absent at `SWEEP_SHA` is reported as not found, never silently dropped.

## Step 2 -- guidance payloads

- `policy` with `{ text, baseSha }`; `text` is the `REVIEW.md` content at `SWEEP_SHA` (`null` when there is none -- the CLI then answers with the strict defaults, which is not the same as no policy).
- `rules` with `{ changedPaths, ruleFiles, rulesFileName, baseSha, sourceSha }`: `changedPaths` is the sweep set, `ruleFiles` every `REVIEW.md` present at `SWEEP_SHA` (from its tree listing), `baseSha` and `sourceSha` both `SWEEP_SHA`.
- `paths` with `{ changedPaths, declaration, codeowners, baseSha }`: `declaration` is `{ sourceSha: <SWEEP_SHA>, sensitive: <policy.sensitivePaths>, high: <policy.highPaths> }` (from the `policy` result) and `codeowners` is the CODEOWNERS text at `SWEEP_SHA`.

The `paths` result's `sensitive` and `high` lists order the sweep (Step 3).

## Step 4 -- depth and slices payloads

- `depth` with `{ tier, requested, bounds, planned }`: `tier` is `TIER` (absent means `high`), `bounds` the policy's override when it carries one, `planned` the `{ reviewers, verifiers }` about to be dispatched.
- `slices` with `{ paths, areas, threshold, mode }`: `paths` is `[{ path, lines }]` for the sweep set (file line counts, since there is no diff), `areas` the directories of the rules files `rules` applied plus the sensitive areas, `threshold` the policy's slice threshold, `mode` the mode `depth` resolved (never typed). `targetLines`, `maxSlices`, `lenses` and `lensesPerSlice` are left out for the default. The result's `reviewerAssignments` (`{ reviewer, sliceId, lens }`, one reviewer per slice and lens) are the reviewer plan: dispatch each with its `sliceId`, `paths` and the brief's `lens`, and pass the list (or its count) as `planned.reviewers` to `depth`. After the review, re-run it with `{ paths, areas, threshold, targetLines?, mode, reviewedBy, changedPaths }`, where `reviewedBy` is the `reviewedBy` array of the `results` `collect` answer (each entry names the `paths` its reviewer read, and a lens counts for those paths only): an `uncovered` path (nobody read it) or an `underReviewed` one (fewer than two distinct lenses at Standard/Deep) is reported as unswept, never as clean. `reviewed` (slice ids) is no longer accepted.

## Step 5 -- reviewer inputs and ledger recording

Each reviewer is given only (1) the files of its slice as at `SWEEP_SHA` (whole files: there is no diff, and "what changed" is not the question), (2) the rules `applied` from Step 2 with the policy and sensitivity facts, (3) the repository guidance a reader would have (README, area `REVIEW.md`), and (4) the `lens` of its `reviewerAssignments` entry, the emphasis it reads the slice under (the reviewer brief carries it). Not the authoring conversation, not this session, not an issue tracker's opinion: a reviewer reading what someone meant stops reviewing what is there.

Ledger entry shape, as in `pr-review-cycle` Step 3: `{ id, source, locationOrLink, severity, failureMode, disposition, evidence, originalTextOrLink }`. Disposition is one of `fix|duplicate|not-applicable|deferred|adjudicate|resolved`; a sweep reports and never fixes, so use `deferred` with a `reason` naming the follow-up issue or report, unless a reviewer marked the candidate `duplicate` or `not-applicable`.

Only `recordRound` normalises `Pre-existing`; `validate` and `dedupe` do not. Run the batch through `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" ledger` with `action: 'recordRound'` and `{ ledger: [], incoming: <candidates>, round: 1 }`; entries in its `findings` come back with `preExisting: true`, and every consumer (report, merge gate, metrics) reads the same fact. Then `action: 'validate'` on the recorded `findings`; a finding missing a required field or carrying an invalid disposition is completed, never dropped. A recorded finding without `preExisting: true` was not tagged: fix its severity and run `recordRound` again before reporting, rather than explaining the tag in the summary.

A sweep still says how bad each finding is: carry the reviewer's own severity judgement in the report (and in `failureMode` and `evidence`), so "pre-existing and serious" is distinguishable from "pre-existing and cosmetic" without re-tagging the finding as something a merge gate must answer.

## Step 6 -- votes payload

`votes` with `{ findings, depth, expectedVerifiers, verificationCapability }`. A `filtered` finding is not reported as something to fix.

## Step 7 -- report contents

`REQUESTED_BY`, `SWEEP_SHA` and the scope as given; the paths examined in band order and the slices reviewed; every verified finding with its band, path and line, severity, `authorLabel` and the **Pre-existing** tag; what was left for the next run (`MAX_PATHS` truncation, uncovered slices, paths not found); the reduced-review notice when verification did not run.

## Recurrence -- the host's template

`/ensemble-init-project` offers to scaffold a workflow template for a weekly sweep -- **opt-in, never written unless the user asks for it** -- and that template is the host's file from the moment it lands: its cron, its runner, its credentials.

- The template needs the host's **own agent credentials** (an API key or token for whichever coding agent runs the review), a secret the repository already has or chooses to add for its own automation.
- The **core review path needs no new CI secret**: `pr-review-cycle`, `pr-merge` and this skill run inside a session a maintainer already authenticated. The sweep workflow is an optional convenience, not a dependency of the review process.

Ensemble ships no `schedule:` trigger of its own; adding one would take ownership of recurrence away from the host repository and from Foreman (Constitution Rule 4).

## Safety rationale

A sweep finding presented without the `Pre-existing` tag reads as a regression someone just introduced -- and would be counted as an open Important finding by the merge gate -- the one misunderstanding this skill exists to prevent.
